Apple___Apple_scab.summary: Apple scab is a fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. It produces scabby spots on leaves and fruit and spreads fastest in cool, wet spring weather.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves
Leaves yellowing and dropping early
Rough, scabby, cracked lesions on fruit
causes: Spores surviving on fallen infected leaves
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn
Prune to open the canopy for airflow
Follow local agriculture office advice on fungicide timing

Apple___Black_rot.summary: Black rot is a fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. It affects leaves, fruit, and branches, and can cause cankers that weaken the tree.
symptoms: Small purple-edged spots on leaves, often called frog-eye spots
Brown rotting areas on fruit that turn black
Sunken, cracked cankers on branches
causes: Infection through dead wood and mummified fruit left on the tree
Warm, wet weather and wounded bark
prevention: Prune out dead wood and cankers
Remove mummified fruit from the tree and ground
Ask a local agriculture officer about fungicide options

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.summary: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. It needs both apple trees and nearby juniper or red cedar to complete its life cycle.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface
Small tube-like structures on the underside of the spots
Leaves dropping early in bad cases
causes: Juniper or red cedar growing near the orchard
Wet spring weather that releases spores
prevention: Remove nearby junipers or cedars where practical
Ask a local agriculture officer about fungicide timing

Apple___healthy.summary: The apple leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Rake up fallen leaves each autumn
Water at the base of the tree

Blueberry___healthy.summary: The blueberry leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Keep soil acidic and well drained
Water at the base of the plant

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.summary: Powdery mildew on cherry is a fungal disease caused by Podosphaera clandestina. It forms a white powdery coating and can distort young leaves and fruit.
symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves
Curled or distorted young leaves
Pale or deformed fruit in severe cases
causes: Warm days and cool humid nights
prevention: Prune to improve airflow and light
Ask a local agriculture officer about fungicide options

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.summary: The cherry leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Water at the base of the tree

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.summary: Gray leaf spot is a fungal disease of maize caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis. It makes rectangular lesions on leaves and can reduce yield in warm, humid conditions.
symptoms: Narrow rectangular grey to tan lesions that follow the leaf veins
Lesions joining together and killing large leaf areas
Lower leaves affected first
causes: Infected crop residue left in the field
Warm, humid weather and repeated maize planting
prevention: Bury or remove crop residue after harvest

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.summary: Common rust is a fungal disease of maize caused by Puccinia sorghi. It produces small rust-coloured pustules on both sides of the leaf.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules turning dark as the season goes on
Leaves yellowing or drying in heavy infections
causes: Spores carried by wind from other fields
prevention: Monitor fields regularly during cool, moist spells
Ask a local agriculture officer about treatment if infection is severe

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.summary: Northern leaf blight is a fungal disease of maize caused by Exserohilum turcicum. It makes long lesions on the leaves and can reduce yield when it starts early.
symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions
Lesions growing and joining together
Leaves drying out from the bottom up
causes: Moderate temperatures with high humidity and heavy dew
prevention: Rotate crops and manage residue after harvest
Ask a local agriculture officer about treatment if infection starts early

Corn_(maize)___healthy.summary: The maize leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms

Grape___Black_rot.summary: Black rot is a fungal disease of grapes caused by Guignardia bidwellii. It can destroy a large part of the crop in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small brown circular spots with dark borders on leaves
Berries turning brown and then shrivelling into hard black mummies
Dark lesions on shoots and stems
causes: Infected mummified berries left on the vine or ground
prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected debris
Prune and train vines for airflow and sun
Ask a local agriculture officer about fungicide timing

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).summary: Esca, also called black measles, is a disease of grapevine wood caused by a group of fungi. It causes striped leaves and spotted berries, and can slowly kill vines.
symptoms: Yellow or red stripes between leaf veins that later turn brown
Dark spots on berries
Sudden wilting of shoots or whole vines in some cases
causes: Wood-decay fungi entering through pruning wounds
Older vines with large pruning wounds
prevention: Prune in dry weather and protect large pruning wounds
Remove and destroy severely affected vines
There is no complete cure, so focus on prevention

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.summary: Leaf blight, also called Isariopsis leaf spot, is a fungal disease of grapes caused by Pseudocercospora vitis. It spots the leaves and can cause early leaf drop.
symptoms: Dark brown angular spots on leaves
Spots joining together on older leaves
Early yellowing and leaf drop
prevention: Prune and train vines for airflow
Ask a local agriculture officer about treatment

Grape___healthy.summary: The grape leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Prune and train vines for airflow and sun
Remove fallen leaves and mummified berries

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).summary: Huanglongbing, also called citrus greening, is a serious bacterial disease of citrus spread by the Asian citrus psyllid. It causes yellow blotchy leaves and bitter, misshapen fruit, and there is no cure.
symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling on leaves that does not follow the veins evenly
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit
Thinning canopy and shoot dieback
causes: Spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect
prevention: Report suspected cases to the local agriculture department

Peach___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial spot is a disease of peach caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni. It spots leaves and fruit and can cause leaves to drop early.
symptoms: Small dark angular spots on leaves, sometimes falling out to leave holes
Yellowing and early leaf drop
Pitted, cracked spots on fruit
causes: Warm, wet, windy weather that spreads bacteria
prevention: Keep trees healthy with balanced feeding and watering
Ask a local agriculture officer about spray options

Peach___healthy.summary: The peach leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Water at the base of the tree
Feed trees in a balanced way

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial spot is a disease of bell pepper caused by Xanthomonas bacteria. It spots leaves and fruit and spreads quickly in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow edges
Leaves yellowing and dropping
Raised scabby spots on fruit
prevention: Use disease-free seed and healthy transplants
Avoid overhead watering and handling wet plants
Ask a local agriculture officer about copper-based options

Pepper,_bell___healthy.summary: The bell pepper leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Water at the base of the plant

Potato___Early_blight.summary: Early blight is a fungal disease of potato caused by Alternaria solani. It spots the older leaves first and can reduce yield if it spreads.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Yellowing around the spots
Leaves drying and dropping early
causes: Infected plant debris in the soil
Warm, humid weather and stressed plants
prevention: Feed and water plants well to avoid stress
Remove infected plant debris after harvest

Potato___Late_blight.summary: Late blight is a fast-spreading disease of potato caused by Phytophthora infestans. It thrives in cool, wet weather and can destroy leaves and tubers quickly, so act fast if you see it.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid weather
Brown, firm rot in tubers
causes: Infected seed tubers and volunteer plants
prevention: Destroy cull piles and volunteer plants
Hill soil well to protect tubers
Contact a local agriculture officer quickly if you see it

Potato___healthy.summary: The potato leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Inspect leaves regularly, especially in wet weather

Raspberry___healthy.summary: The raspberry leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Water at the base of the plant

Soybean___healthy.summary: The soybean leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms

Squash___Powdery_mildew.summary: Powdery mildew is a fungal disease of squash caused mainly by Podosphaera xanthii. It forms a white powdery coating on leaves and can weaken the plant.
symptoms: White powdery patches on the upper leaf surface
Patches spreading to cover whole leaves
Leaves yellowing, drying, and dying early
prevention: Water the soil rather than the leaves

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.summary: Leaf scorch is a fungal disease of strawberry caused by Diplocarpon earlianum. It spots the leaves and can weaken plants over time.
symptoms: Many small purple spots on leaves
Spots enlarging with brown centres
Badly affected leaves looking scorched and dry
causes: Infected old leaves and plant debris
Warm, wet weather and crowded plants
prevention: Remove old infected leaves after harvest

Strawberry___healthy.summary: The strawberry leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Water at the base of the plant

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.summary: Bacterial spot is a disease of tomato caused by Xanthomonas bacteria. It spots leaves and fruit and spreads quickly in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves, often with yellow edges
Spots drying and leaving ragged holes
Raised scabby spots on fruit
causes: Splashing rain, overhead watering, and handling wet plants
prevention: Use disease-free seed and healthy transplants
Avoid overhead watering and working among wet plants
Ask a local agriculture officer about copper-based options

Tomato___Early_blight.summary: Early blight is a fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. It mostly starts on older, lower leaves and can reduce yield if it spreads.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
Yellowing around the spots
Leaves drying and dropping early
causes: Infected plant debris left in the soil
prevention: Water at the base, not over the leaves
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves

Tomato___Late_blight.summary: Late blight is a fast-spreading disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. It thrives in cool, wet conditions and can destroy a crop quickly.
symptoms: Water-soaked, grey-green patches on leaves
White fuzzy growth on the underside in humid weather
Brown, firm rot on fruit
causes: Spread by wind and rain from infected plants

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.summary: Leaf mold is a fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva. It is most common in humid, poorly ventilated conditions such as greenhouses.
symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to grey velvety mold on the underside
Leaves curling and withering
causes: Leaves staying wet for long periods

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.summary: Septoria leaf spot is a fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici. It makes many small spots on the lower leaves and can strip a plant of leaves in wet weather.
symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres
Tiny black dots inside the spots
Lower leaves yellowing and dropping first
causes: Warm, wet weather and splashing water
prevention: Mulch and water at the base of the plant
Space and stake plants for airflow

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.summary: Two-spotted spider mites are tiny pests, not a disease. They suck sap from the leaves and thrive in hot, dry, dusty conditions.
symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckles on leaves
Fine webbing on the underside of leaves
Leaves bronzing, drying, and dropping
causes: Hot, dry weather and dusty conditions
Plants stressed by lack of water
prevention: Keep plants well watered and reduce dust
Ask a local agriculture officer about suitable miticide or soap options

Tomato___Target_Spot.summary: Target spot is a fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola. It makes ringed spots on leaves and sometimes fruit, and is common in warm, humid weather.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings, often with a yellow edge
Spots joining and killing leaf areas
Sunken spots on fruit in some cases
causes: Warm, humid weather with long leaf wetness
prevention: Space and prune plants for airflow

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.summary: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus is a virus spread by whiteflies. It stunts plants, curls and yellows the leaves, and reduces fruit, and there is no cure once a plant is infected.
symptoms: Leaves curling upward and turning yellow
Stunted, bushy plant growth
Few flowers and poor fruit set
causes: Whitefly populations building up in warm weather
prevention: Control whiteflies using nets, traps, and advice from a local agriculture officer
Remove and destroy infected plants early

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.summary: Tomato mosaic virus is a virus that spreads easily by touch, tools, and seed. It causes mottled, distorted leaves and can lower yield, and there is no cure.
symptoms: Light and dark green mottling on leaves
Leaves twisted, narrow, or distorted
Stunted plants and uneven fruit ripening
causes: Spread by hands, tools, and contaminated seed
Virus surviving on plant debris and surfaces
prevention: Wash hands and disinfect tools between plants
Wash hands after handling tobacco before touching plants

Tomato___healthy.summary: The tomato leaf looks healthy, with no clear signs of disease in this image.
symptoms: No visible disease symptoms
prevention: Water at the base of the plant
